sources.relevant_excerpt:
Relying entirely on an attention mechanism,
the Transformer introduced by Vaswani et
al. (2017) achieves state-of-the-art results for
machine translation. In contrast to recurrent
and convolutional neural networks, it does
not explicitly model relative or absolute po-
sition information in its structure.
Instead,
it requires adding representations of abso-
lute positions to its inputs.
In this work
we present an alternative approach, extend-
ing the self-attention mechanism to efﬁciently
consider representations of the relative posi-
tions, or distances between sequence elements.
On the WMT 2014 English-to-German and
English-to-French translation tasks, this ap-
proach yields improvements of 1.3 BLEU and
0.3 BLEU over absolute position representa-
tions, respectively. Notably, we observe that
combining relative and absolute position rep-
resentations yields no further improvement in
translation quality.
We describe an efﬁcient
implementation of our method and cast it as an
instance of relation-aware self-attention mech-
anisms that can generalize to arbitrary graph-
labeled inputs.

observations.original_excerpt:
Relying entirely on an attention mechanism,
the Transformer introduced by Vaswani et
al. (2017) achieves state-of-the-art results for
machine translation. In contrast to recurrent
and convolutional neural networks, it does
not explicitly model relative or absolute po-
sition information in its structure.
Instead,
it requires adding representations of abso-
lute positions to its inputs.
In this work
we present an alternative approach, extend-
ing the self-attention mechanism to efﬁciently
consider representations of the relative posi-
tions, or distances between sequence elements.
On the WMT 2014 English-to-German and
English-to-French translation tasks, this ap-
proach yields improvements of 1.3 BLEU and
0.3 BLEU over absolute position representa-
tions, respectively. Notably, we observe that
combining relative and absolute position rep-
resentations yields no further improvement in
translation quality.
We describe an efﬁcient
implementation of our method and cast it as an
instance of relation-aware self-attention mech-
anisms that can generalize to arbitrary graph-
labeled inputs.

adjudications.original_central_question: Were each absolute-position baseline and its corresponding relative-position model trained, selected, decoded, and evaluated under matched conditions so that the reported BLEU differences can be attributed to the position representations?

fact_assessments.original_observed_fact: The authors state that they generated baseline results to isolate the impact of relative position representations from other changes to the library and experimental configuration. The reported model settings nevertheless differ between base and big configurations: the base model is trained for 100,000 steps without checkpoint averaging on K40 GPUs, whereas the big model is trained for 300,000 steps with the last 20 checkpoints averaged on P100 GPUs. The supplied units do not give complete, separate baseline training and checkpoint-selection details.
fact_assessments.explanation: The frozen excerpts and extracted text explicitly state the baseline-generation rationale and the listed base/big training differences. They do not separately enumerate baseline-specific training and checkpoint-selection procedures, but whether the general configuration descriptions also cover the baselines is unclear. The incompleteness judgment is an inference; differences between model sizes do not establish a mismatch between each proposed model and its corresponding baseline.

fact_assessments.original_observed_fact: The authors state that they generated sinusoidal-position baseline results to isolate relative position representations from changes to the underlying library and experimental configuration. They report base and big model configurations, including different training durations, hardware, dropout settings, clipping distances, and checkpoint averaging procedures for the proposed models.
fact_assessments.explanation: The frozen excerpts and extracted text support this summary of the authors' rationale and reported configurations. Dropout differs between base and big for EN-DE, while both use 0.1 for EN-FR; clipping distances are explicitly conditional on using relative position encodings. These descriptions do not establish baseline/proposed-model configuration mismatches.
